Texas Tech High School: As a full-time Texas Tech K-12 high school student, you must maintain academic progress in a minimum of four courses concurrently. Note: you will need to take more than the minimum number of courses to stay on grade level and graduate at your desired time.

How do I get started with a Course or Credit By Exam (CBE)?

Available Courses and Credit By Exam's may be viewed via the Course Catalog (opens in new tab). Prior to enrolling, we ask that you please confirm with your local school that they will award credit for the course. Upon completion of the course, student's will be ale to view the overall course grade in the portal. You may also print out a copy of the grade report.

Can I retake the CBE Exam if I fail my first attempt?

According to Texas state law, students are only allowed two attempts per CBE for the same subject. After two attempts, the student must take the full course. To accommodate this requirement Texas Tech K-12 provides two separate versions of each Credit by Exam.

Please enroll in the Set 1 version for the first attempt. If the student passes Set 1, no Set 2 is needed. However, in the event the student fails or does not make the required grade on the Set 1 exam, they may enroll in the Set 2 version for the second attempt.

Credit by Exams are non-refundable. CBE’s cannot be extended. If not taken prior to the expiration date, students must purchase another CBE or enroll in the course.

Can I retake the CBE Exam if I fail my first attempt?

According to Texas state law, students are only allowed two attempts per CBE for the same subject. After two attempts, the student must take the full course. To accommodate this requirement Texas Tech K-12 provides two separate versions of each Credit by Exam.

Please enroll in the Set 1 version for the first attempt. If the student passes Set 1, no Set 2 is needed. However, in the event the student fails or does not make the required grade on the Set 1 exam, they may enroll in the Set 2 version for the second attempt.

Can I retake the CBE Exam if I fail my first attempt?

According to Texas state law, students are only allowed two attempts per CBE for the same subject. After two attempts, the student must take the full course. To accommodate this requirement Texas Tech K-12 provides two separate versions of each Credit by Exam.

Please enroll in the Set 1 version for the first attempt. If the student passes Set 1, no Set 2 is needed. However, in the event the student fails or does not make the required grade on the Set 1 exam, they may enroll in the Set 2 version for the second attempt.

Credit by Exams are non-refundable. CBE’s cannot be extended. If not taken prior to the expiration date, students must purchase another CBE or enroll in the course.

Please refer to our policies (opens in new tab) and student handbook (opens in new tab) for more information.

Key Policies

Two Attempts Only: Per Texas law, students can attempt the same CBE only twice. After that, they must take the full course.

Two Versions: Each CBE has a Set 1 and a Set 2.

Step 1: Take Set 1 first.

Step 2: If unsuccessful, enroll in Set 2 for the second attempt.

Step 3: Do not enroll in the same version twice.

Important: CBEs are non-refundable and cannot be extended. If the exam expires without being taken, students must purchase a new CBE or enroll in the full course.

This policy covers any generative Artificial Intelligence tool, such as Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer (ChatGPT), Elicit, Photo Math, etc. This includes text and artwork/graphics/video/audio, etc.

All work submitted in this course must be your own. You may not use artificial intelligence tools to complete your assignments in this course.

If an instructor suspects that an assignment is not the work of the student, it will receive a score of zero. The instructor will message the student or provide feedback on the assignment indicating the need to schedule a one-on-one video conference, during which the student will be required to demonstrate their skills or knowledge through an alternative or mutually agreed-upon assignment. The grade of the alternate or agreed upon assignment will be determined at the instructor’s discretion with the highest possible score being 70%.

If it is determined that a student has violated final exam directions on Final Exam A or Credit By Exam Set 1, the exam will be scored as zero. The student may take Final Exam B or Credit By Exam Set 2 with the highest possible score being 70%.

The incident will be reported to Texas Tech K-12 Administration and documented in the student’s file. Continued violations of Texas Tech University’s Academic Integrity Policy will result in the removal of the student from the program. Texas Tech Student Handbook (opens in new tab).

Key Policies

Two Attempts Only: Per Texas law, students can attempt the same CBE only twice. After that, they must take the full course.

Two Versions: Each CBE has a Set 1 and a Set 2.

Step 1: Take Set 1 first.

Step 2: If unsuccessful, enroll in Set 2 for the second attempt.

Step 3: Do not enroll in the same version twice.

Important: CBEs are non-refundable and cannot be extended. If the exam expires without being taken, students must purchase a new CBE or enroll in the full course.

Policy EHDC (Local) - Alternative Methods for Earning Credit: Credit by Examination Without Prior Instruction

Examinations for Acceleration or Course Credit

All methods of student acceleration must be approved prior to attempt by the student’s Texas Tech K-12 Advisor.

If a student in grades K-8 wishes to accelerate to the next grade level or a student in grades 6-12 wishes to earn course credit without having received prior instruction in the grade level or course, the District shall offer opportunities in accordance with state law and State Board rules for the student to take a Board-approved examination for this purpose. Students shall have the opportunity to accelerate and earn course credit without prior instruction by demonstrating proficiency on a Texas Tech University credit by examination (CBE) assessment with a minimum score of 80%.

Grades 1-5

The student must be recommended for acceleration by a district representative, and the student’s parent or guardian must give written permission.

A student in grades 1-5 may be accelerated one grade level if the student scores 80% or higher on each of the language arts, mathematics, science, and social studies CBE assessments for the grade level the student wishes to accelerate through.

Acceleration in a single subject area is allowed in accordance with local policy.

A student may not accelerate two consecutive grade levels or single subject area levels by Credit By Exam assessments.

Online instruction presents different challenges than those in a traditional classroom. The curriculum is rigorous and is reading- and writing-intensive. Successful online students are able to take initiative and manage their own time.

Q: How does only ranking the Top 10% benefit students in the top quarter of students who are very close to the Top 10%?

A: When a student does not have a rank, a college will conduct a holistic review of the student's college application, examining the rigor of courses taken, grades received, SAT/ACT scores, and other factors. This is beneficial to Texas Tech K-12 students just outside the Top 10% because these students, along with many other districts' students, have high grades, high test scores, and strong academic and extra-curricular achievement. Many colleges generate a rank based on these factors. School counselors of other high performing schools that do not rank, report the college assigned rank tends to be higher than the high school generated rank would have been.

Understanding the Texas Success Initiative Assessment Test

The current Texas Success Initiative Assessment test is version two, commonly referred to as TSIA2. TSIA2 was administered for any student taking the test after Jan. 11, 2021, and replaced the original Texas Success Initiative Assessment test (TSIA).

Before taking TSIA2, students are required to participate in a Pre-Assessment Activity (opens in new tab). The activity will explain some of the test procedures and provide practice test questions along with feedback on answers to the practice questions. The activity also will provide options and campus resources to help them meet minimum standards.

Step 1: The Texas Success Initiative Assessment in Mathematics contains a multiple-choice assessment with approximately 20 items on the placement test and 10 items in each section of the diagnostic test. Students with passing scores on the placement test will not be required to take the diagnostic test.

Step 2: The Texas Success Initiative Assessment in Reading contains multiple choice with approximately 24 questions in the placement test and 10-12 items in each section of the diagnostic test.

Step 3: The Texas Success Initiative Assessment in Writing contains a multiple-choice section and an essay section. There are approximately 24 items in the placement test and 10-12 items per section in the diagnostic test. What is Texas Success Initiative?

Texas Success Initiative (opens in new tab) (TSI) is a state-legislated program designed to improve student success at the college level. The Texas Success Initiative Assessment test helps determine if a student admitted to college is prepared to take college-level coursework in Reading, Writing and mathematics. Incoming college students in Texas are required to take the Texas Success Initiative Assessment unless they are exempt and will either be placed in college-level courses or placed in a developmental course depending on their assessment test scores.

What scores do I need to pass?

The minimum passing standards for the TSIA2 require a College Readiness Classification (CRC) score of at least 950 or a College Readiness Classification score below 950 and a diagnostic level of 6 for Mathematics. A College Readiness Classification score of at least 945 and an essay score of at least 5, or a College Readiness Classification score below 945 and a diagnostic level of 5 or 6, and an essay score of at least 5 are required for the English Language Arts Reading (ELAR) test.

For students who took the original TSIA, the standards are slightly different and require a score of 351 or higher on Reading, a score of 340 or higher and an essay score of 4 or higher for Writing, and a score of 350 or higher for Math.

Texas Tech Middle School Program Requirements

Texas Tech Middle School: As a full-time Texas Tech K-12 middle school student, you must maintain academic progress in a minimum of four courses concurrently.

Students enrolled in Texas Tech Middle School should complete four to five subject areas (eight to ten Texas Tech K-12 courses) per calendar year. The following table outlines courses required in each grade:

Step 1: Students must complete a semester course in Career Exploration (CE) between the seventh and eighth grades.

Understanding the Texas Success Initiative Assessment Test

The current Texas Success Initiative Assessment test is version two, commonly referred to as TSIA2. TSIA2 was administered for any student taking the test after Jan. 11, 2021, and replaced the original Texas Success Initiative Assessment test (TSIA).

Before taking TSIA2, students are required to participate in a Pre-Assessment Activity (opens in new tab). The activity will explain some of the test procedures and provide practice test questions along with feedback on answers to the practice questions. The activity also will provide options and campus resources to help them meet minimum standards.

Step 1: The Texas Success Initiative Assessment in Mathematics contains a multiple-choice assessment with approximately 20 items on the placement test and 10 items in each section of the diagnostic test. Students with passing scores on the placement test will not be required to take the diagnostic test.

Step 2: The Texas Success Initiative Assessment in Reading contains multiple choice with approximately 24 questions in the placement test and 10-12 items in each section of the diagnostic test.

Step 3: The Texas Success Initiative Assessment in Writing contains a multiple-choice section and an essay section. There are approximately 24 items in the placement test and 10-12 items per section in the diagnostic test. For the essay section, students are asked to write a five-paragraph essay on an issue of current interest.

Texas Tech High School: As a full-time Texas Tech K-12 high school student, you must maintain academic progress in a minimum of four courses concurrently. Note: you will need to take more than the minimum number of courses to stay on grade level and graduate at your desired time.

**Texas Success Initiative (TSI) Requirements**

The Texas Success Initiative (TSI) is a state-legislated program aimed at improving student success at the college level. Here are the key details:

- **Assessment Requirement**: Incoming college students in Texas must take the Texas Success Initiative Assessment (TSIA2) unless they qualify for an exemption. This assessment evaluates readiness for college-level coursework in Reading, Writing, and Mathematics.

- **Passing Scores**:
  - **Mathematics**: A College Readiness Classification (CRC) score of at least 950, or a score below 950 with a diagnostic level of 6.
  - **English Language Arts Reading (ELAR)**: A CRC score of at least 945 and an essay score of at least 5, or a score below 945 with a diagnostic level of 5 or 6, and an essay score of at least 5.

- **Exemptions**: Students may be exempt from taking the TSIA2 if they meet specific criteria, such as achieving certain scores on the ACT, SAT, or STAAR exams, or transferring from another institution with completed college-level coursework.

- **Pre-Assessment Activity**: Before taking the TSIA2, students must complete a Pre-Assessment Activity, which includes test procedures and practice questions.

For further details on TSI requirements or exemptions, you can contact the Texas Tech K-12 program at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

What is Texas Success Initiative?

Texas Success Initiative (opens in new tab) (TSI) is a state-legislated program designed to improve student success at the college level. The Texas Success Initiative Assessment test helps determine if a student admitted to college is prepared to take college-level coursework in Reading, Writing and mathematics. Incoming college students in Texas are required to take the Texas Success Initiative Assessment unless they are exempt and will either be placed in college-level courses or placed in a developmental course depending on their assessment test scores.

Understanding the Texas Success Initiative Assessment Test

The current Texas Success Initiative Assessment test is version two, commonly referred to as TSIA2. TSIA2 was administered for any student taking the test after Jan. 11, 2021, and replaced the original Texas Success Initiative Assessment test (TSIA).

Before taking TSIA2, students are required to participate in a Pre-Assessment Activity (opens in new tab). The activity will explain some of the test procedures and provide practice test questions along with feedback on answers to the practice questions. The activity also will provide options and campus resources to help them meet minimum standards.

Step 1: The Texas Success Initiative Assessment in Mathematics contains a multiple-choice assessment with approximately 20 items on the placement test and 10 items in each section of the diagnostic test. Students with passing scores on the placement test will not be required to take the diagnostic test.

Step 2: The Texas Success Initiative Assessment in Reading contains multiple choice with approximately 24 questions in the placement test and 10-12 items in each section of the diagnostic test.

Step 3: The Texas Success Initiative Assessment in Writing contains a multiple-choice section and an essay section. There are approximately 24 items in the placement test and 10-12 items per section in the diagnostic test. For the essay section, students are asked to write a five-paragraph essay on an issue of current interest.

To graduate with a Texas Tech High School diploma, you will take at least your last year of high school credits (25%) from Texas Tech K-12. Exceptions will be considered by administration on a case-by-case basis but the last semester (2.5 credits) must be taken from Texas Tech K-12.

**Registering for Advanced Placement (AP) Exams**

For full-time Texas Tech K-12 students, registering for AP exams involves the following steps:

1. **Find a Nearby Testing School**: Since Texas Tech K-12 does not offer in-person testing, students must arrange to take the AP exam at a local school.

2. **Contact the AP Coordinator**: Reach out to the Advanced Placement Coordinator at the chosen school to inquire if they allow outside testers.

3. **Follow Registration Procedures**: Adhere to the school's registration process, deadlines, and pay any required fees. Schools typically place AP exam orders with the College Board in early November, so it's important to contact them no later than October 31.

4. **Enroll in Exam-Only Section**: You may need to enroll in the school's "exam only" course section while remaining enrolled in your Texas Tech K-12 course section.

Texas Tech K-12 High School Program - Full-Time

Texas Tech K-12 is a state-approved option for students who need or desire the flexibility of a distance education to earn their high school diploma. We offer all courses necessary to meet the requirements to complete a Texas high school graduation plan.

Why Texas Tech K-12?

Texas Tech K-12 is fully accredited by the Texas Education Agency (TEA) and approved by the National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA). We provide the same rigorous academic standards as traditional schools, but with the flexibility to learn from anywhere at any time. Our online programs cover elementary, middle and high school, and we offer tailored options for individual students as well as entire classes or cohorts.

International Program

At Texas Tech K-12, we are committed to expanding educational opportunities worldwide by forming international partnerships with schools that are eager to provide innovative learning experiences. Whether you're a student, parent or school administrator, we're here to offer flexible, high-quality educational options that fit your needs.

Supplemental Program Information

Anyone looking to supplement their current school curriculum or home school curriculum can enroll in Texas Tech K-12.  Our Texas Tech K-12 Supplemental Program (opens in new tab) is designed to allow students in elementary, middle and high school that allows students to work at their own pace. We have students who must do their work at home for various reasons, such as travel "outside" of the U.S. for extended amounts of time, have health issues, are actors, entertainers, and athletes who cannot fit the traditional schooling into their schedule. We have school all year and do not keep a traditional academic schedule, so it is possible to move through our program faster than the typical semester-based programs.

This is a self-paced program where all the instructional content is provided. The courses tend to be reading and writing intensive. Online courses require self-discipline and excellent time-management skills. The courses are not virtual classrooms and do not require any interaction with any other students or instructors. Each course has lessons, which are like chapters, and a final exam. The final exam will be proctored online by an online proctoring service.

Texas Tech K-12 uses the guidelines below to compute your final Grade Point Average (GPA) in Texas Tech High School:

Step 1: Texas Tech K-12 computes the Grade Point Average for graduation using all accredited Texas Tech K-12 courses that apply to graduation

Step 2: Each numerical grade will be assigned the following points:

Grade to Points Conversion | Grade to Points Conversion | Grade to Points Conversion | Grade to Points Conversion

------------------------------------------------------------

Numerical Grade | Alphabetic Grade | Points for Regular Courses | Points for Honors, Advanced Placement, and Dual Credit Courses

90-100 | A | 4.0 | 5.0

80-89 | B | 3.0 | 4.0

75-79 | C | 2.0 | 3.0

70-74 | D | 1.0 | 2.0

0-69 | F | 0.0 | 0.0

All course grades while you are enrolled in Texas Tech K-12 will be recorded on your transcript and used in computing your final Grade Point Average. However, you may replace a failing grade you received on a Texas Tech K-12 course or Credit By Exam by repeating the course or Credit By Exam.

Transfer Grades for the High School Program

All grades transferred to Texas Tech High School from another accredited school will be used in computing your final Grade Point Average except for local credit courses and courses scored on a pass/fail scale.

Grades on homeschool transcripts and transcripts from non-accredited schools are not transferable. To receive credit for non-accredited courses, you must take Credit by Exams (CBEs) or enroll in the courses.

If you have failed a previous transfer course, you may repeat the course for credit with Texas Tech High School.

chunks.text:
Q: If I have more questions about class rank, how do I ask?

A. You may submit your questions via submit a request (opens in a new tab).

Q: What is class rank?

A: Class rank is a student's standing among others of the same year based on a numeric grade point average (GPA). (Collins English Dictionary) Class rank places all students in numerical order based solely on how their GPAs compare to one another.

Q: How will students know if they are close to being in the Top 10% of their class?

A: The cut point of the weighted grade point average (GPA) used to determine class rank earned by a student currently in the Top 10% of the class shall be Texas Tech K-12 Class Rank Frequently Asked Questions 2021-2022 communicated to all students in each class in January and June of the sophomore, junior, and senior year.

Graduation

For our Full-Time students, the graduation tab will show which endorsement your student has selected, along with their State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness (STAAR) and End of Course (EOC) Mastery scores.

Grad Reqs (Full-Time Students Only)

The Graduation Requirements Report will show how many credits you will need to complete your High School Diploma.

Clicking on "Show Detailed" will show which classes have been used for the credits:

Q: How does this impact admissions to universities?

A: In high performing school districts like TTU K-12, students who rank outside the top 10% would normally rank very high at other districts. This can hurt our students in college admissions. If a student has been given a rank by a high school, for example, the 40th percentile, many universities will use that rank as a shortcut to evaluate the student and say that student falls in the top 40% of all applicants to the university. However, if the student does not have a high school rank, the university will evaluate the student's record and assign them a rank relative to other applicants. When compared to other college applicants, our students tend to be more qualified than those who graduate with a similar ranking at other high schools. According to other Texas districts, schools saw a 38% increase in acceptance to the University of Texas and a 49% increase to Texas A&M after eliminating class rank.

WHAT HAPPENS IF I CANNOT BE THERE TO TEST?

If you are ill or have an emergency, please contact your testing coordinator immediately. To ensure that you remain on schedule to graduate, participation in and successful completion of both State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness and State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness/End Of Course is necessary and is a condition of your enrollment with Texas Tech K-12. Failure to test will result in removal from the tuition-free program per our attendance policy.

Identification Cards and Verification of Enrollment (VOE)

You may request a Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) Verification of Enrollment and Attendance Form or an official letter verifying enrollment and attendance from your Texas Tech K-12 academic advisor. Texas Tech K-12 administration may deny verification of enrollment and attendance to any student who has not maintained adequate progress to stay on grade level. Request a Verification of Enrollment and Attendance by emailing a request to your Texas Tech K-12 academic advisor. The advisor will require at least two working days for progress review.

If you are denied a Verification of Enrollment and Attendance, your Texas Tech K-12 academic advisor will work with you to outline a progress intervention plan to meet the requirements necessary to receive a Verification of Enrollment and Attendance in the future.

Q: Why rank only the top 10% of students?

A: The National Association for College Admissions Counseling states that more than half of all high schools no longer report student rankings. The percentage of school districts across the country not ranking students is increasing each year for a variety of reasons, including the following: class rank may not accurately reflect academic TTU K-12 Class Rank FAQ 2021-2022 achievement, discourages students from taking non-weighted classes in which they are interested, does not have a standardized methodology across districts, and allows colleges to label students without looking at their full academic-achievement record.

Graduation (Full-time Students Only)

Graduation will allow you to see the graduation plan for your student (Full-time Students Only).

Q: If Texas Tech K-12 is a non-ranking district, will call rank appear on transcripts or in the Focus Student Information System?

A: Class rank will not be printed on students' transcripts. Class rank will not appear in Focus.

Q: Are Texas high schools required to publicize student class rank?

A: Schools are not required to publish class rank information. In accordance with Texas Education Code (TEC) §28.026, and Texas Administrative Code (TAC) §61.1201, school districts are required to provide written notification of eligibility for automatic college admission under the Uniform Admission Policy TEC §51.803.

Class Rank

Beginning with 9th grade students enrolling in Texas Tech K-12 after August 1, 2021, class rank will not be calculated or reported except of students in the Top 10% of a given class as required by state law.

Q: Without having a class rank, what factors are most important for college admissions?

A:Without a class rank, college admissions officers will look more closely at applications and high school transcripts. Important factors will include the following: maintaining a high grade point average, college entrance exams (SAT and ACT), challenging school course selections, extracurricular involvement, college application essays, and personal recommendations.

**Passing a Course Without Passing the Final Exam**

In the Texas Tech K-12 program, the course grade is calculated with 50% from the coursework average and 50% from the summative assessment average, which includes the final exam. To pass a course, a student must achieve a course grade of 70 or higher. Therefore, it is possible for a student to pass the course without passing the final exam if their coursework average is sufficiently high to offset a lower final exam score.

Students who score below 70% on their first final exam attempt can retake the exam once, providing another chance to improve their overall course grade.

answer.text:
**Conversion and Posting of Dual Credit Grades**

For Texas Tech K-12 students, dual credit grades are converted and posted as follows:

- **Grade Conversion**: Dual credit courses are graded on a college scale, and these grades are converted to the high school scale for inclusion on the Texas Tech K-12 transcript. A "C" or higher in a Texas Tech University dual credit course is required to award high school credit.

- **Weighted Credits**: Dual credit courses receive weighted credits when calculating the Grade Point Average (GPA). For example, a grade in the range of 90-100 in a dual credit course is assigned 5.0 points, compared to 4.0 points for regular courses.

- **Transcript Posting**: Once the dual credit course is completed and the grade is received, it is recorded on the student's official Texas Tech K-12 transcript. All accredited courses that apply to graduation are used to compute the GPA, excluding any approved PE Substitution (SUBPRO) credits and local credit courses.

For more detailed information or specific questions about dual credit grades, you can contact TTU K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

Policy EHDC (Local) - Alternative Methods for Earning Credit: Credit by Examination Without Prior Instruction

Examinations for Acceleration or Course Credit

All methods of student acceleration must be approved prior to attempt by the student’s Texas Tech K-12 Advisor.

If a student in grades K-8 wishes to accelerate to the next grade level or a student in grades 6-12 wishes to earn course credit without having received prior instruction in the grade level or course, the District shall offer opportunities in accordance with state law and State Board rules for the student to take a Board-approved examination for this purpose. Students shall have the opportunity to accelerate and earn course credit without prior instruction by demonstrating proficiency on a Texas Tech University credit by examination (CBE) assessment with a minimum score of 80%.

Can I retake the CBE Exam if I fail my first attempt?

According to Texas state law, students are only allowed two attempts per CBE for the same subject. After two attempts, the student must take the full course. To accommodate this requirement Texas Tech K-12 provides two separate versions of each Credit by Exam.

Please enroll in the Set 1 version for the first attempt. If the student passes Set 1, no Set 2 is needed. However, in the event the student fails or does not make the required grade on the Set 1 exam, they may enroll in the Set 2 version for the second attempt.

Credit by Exams are non-refundable. CBE’s cannot be extended. If not taken prior to the expiration date, students must purchase another CBE or enroll in the course.

Yes, you can transfer to a different course within the Texas Tech K-12 program. Here’s how you can do it:

**Transferring Records When Withdrawing from the Full-Time Program**

When withdrawing from the Texas Tech K-12 full-time program, you will need to ensure that your student's records are transferred to their new school. Here’s how you can proceed:

1. **Submit a Withdrawal Request**: Use the Program Withdrawal/Change Request form to officially withdraw from the program.

Minimum Lesson/Unit Completion Requirements

Students demonstrate attendance in Texas Tech K-12 online school by regularly completing assignments. Attendance is directly tied to what the student accomplishes and/or produces over a given period. The assignments completed are the evidence that a student has been in attendance, and if no work is produced, then a student is not considered to be in attendance.

Unless specifically stated otherwise, attendance is required a minimum of 3 days per week. A student must complete at least 5% of course assignments in a seven-day period and in every subsequent seven-day period until the course is completed.

Course completion is required to earn course credit. No partial course credit will be granted. Course credit is earned when the student has successfully demonstrated mastery of the Texas Essential Knowledge and Skills for the course.

Students have six months from the date of enrollment to complete each course. To remain in the program, students must be concurrently enrolled in a minimum of four courses.

Failure to meet minimum progress requirements may cause Texas Tech K-12 to implement truancy processes and may result in your removal from the program.

**Troubleshooting Portal Login Issues**

If you're having trouble logging into the Texas Tech K-12 Focus Portal or your password reset isn't working, here are some steps you can take:

1. **Check Your Credentials**: Ensure that you are entering the correct username and password. If you've forgotten your password, use the "Forgot Password" link to initiate a reset.

2. **Password Reset**: If the password reset isn't working, make sure you are using the correct email address associated with your account. Texas Tech K-12 requires unique email addresses for each user, so ensure that the email isn't shared with another account.

3. **Account Lockout**: After five unsuccessful login attempts, your account may be locked for two hours. Wait for this period to pass before trying again.

4. **Contact Support**: If issues persist, contact Texas Tech K-12 support for assistance. You can reach them at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

**Troubleshooting Password Reset Issues**

If a student is unable to reset their password for the Texas Tech K-12 portal, here are some steps they can take:

1. **Check Email Address**: Ensure that the email address used for the password reset is the one associated with the student's account. Texas Tech K-12 requires a unique email address for each student, and it cannot be shared with a parent or another student.

2. **Follow Password Requirements**: When creating a new password, make sure it meets the following criteria:
   - At least 12 characters long
   - Includes both uppercase and lowercase letters
   - Contains at least one numeric character
   - Includes at least one special character

3. **Contact Support**: If the issue persists, contact Texas Tech K-12 support for assistance. They can help resolve login issues and ensure the account is accessible. You can reach them at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

What Information Does Proctorio Collect From Students?

Unlike other online proctoring services, Proctorio does not employ the use of biometrics or external human proctors to monitor the student while they take the exam. Proctorio will record the student’s identity via webcam and, depending upon the exam settings, monitor the exam attempt in various ways. A multitude of privacy provisions have been established to ensure student privacy and FERPA compliance.

Step 1: Proctorio has no file access of any kind. Proctorio cannot and will not access any of personnel files or documents.

Step 2: During an exam Proctorio may take screenshots of the desktop, detect the number of computer monitors connected to the computer, or record web traffic. The information is stored with zero-knowledge encryption, which means the data is encrypted both in transit and at rest.

1. **Check Your Email**: Ensure you have received the email with the access code for your e-textbook. This email can sometimes take between 48 to 72 hours to arrive after purchase.

**Troubleshooting Missing Classes or App in the Parent Portal**

If a student's classes or app aren't showing in the Texas Tech K-12 Parent Portal, here are some steps to resolve the issue:

1. **Check Account Connection**: Ensure that the student's account is properly connected to the Parent Portal. If the student is not showing, you may need to connect the student's account via the Parent Portal by selecting "I would like to Add a Child who is already enrolled."

2. **Verify Enrollment**: Confirm that the student is enrolled in the courses and that the enrollment process is complete. This can be done by checking the student's status in the Focus portal.

3. **Browser Compatibility**: Ensure you are using a compatible browser, such as Google Chrome, and that any necessary extensions, like Adobe Acrobat, are enabled.

4. **Contact Support**: If the issue persists, contact Texas Tech K-12 support for assistance. They can help troubleshoot and ensure that the student's information is correctly displayed in the portal. You can reach them at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

**Troubleshooting Zoom Session Issues for TTU K-12 Students**

If a student is having trouble opening Zoom sessions, here are some steps to resolve the issue:

1. **Check Internet Connection**: Ensure that the student has a stable internet connection. A wired connection is preferred for better stability.

2. **Update Zoom**: Make sure that the Zoom application is updated to the latest version. Outdated software can cause compatibility issues.

3. **Browser Compatibility**: If accessing Zoom through a browser, ensure that the browser is up to date. Google Chrome is recommended for the best experience.

4. **Clear Cache and Cookies**: Sometimes clearing the browser's cache and cookies can resolve loading issues.

5. **Firewall and Security Settings**: Check if any firewall or security settings are blocking Zoom. Adjust settings to allow Zoom to run.

6. **Restart the Device**: A simple restart of the computer or device can sometimes resolve technical issues.

7. **Contact Support**: If the problem persists, contact Texas Tech K-12 support for further assistance. You can reach them at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

**Troubleshooting Course Links in the Learning Management System (LMS)**

If course links inside the Texas Tech K-12 Learning Management System (LMS) aren't loading, try the following steps:

1. **Check Internet Connection**: Ensure you have a stable internet connection. A wired connection is often more reliable than Wi-Fi.

2. **Browser Compatibility**: Use a compatible browser, such as Google Chrome, and ensure it is updated to the latest version.

3. **Clear Cache and Cookies**: Sometimes clearing your browser's cache and cookies can resolve loading issues.

4. **Disable Browser Extensions**: Some extensions may interfere with the LMS. Try disabling them temporarily to see if it resolves the issue.

5. **Try a Different Browser**: If the problem persists, try accessing the LMS using a different browser to see if the issue is browser-specific.

**Troubleshooting Course Links in the LMS**

If Canvas isn't showing in the student's account, it could be linked to an unconfirmed student email or other technical issues. Here are some steps to resolve the problem:

1. **Confirm Email Address**: Ensure that the student's email address is confirmed and correctly associated with their account. An unconfirmed email can sometimes lead to access issues.

2. **Check Browser Compatibility**: Use a compatible browser such as Google Chrome, Firefox, Edge, or Safari. Ensure the browser is updated to the latest version.

3. **Enable Necessary Settings**: Make sure JavaScript, cookies, and pop-ups are enabled in the browser settings. Disable any ad blockers that might interfere with loading content.

4. **Clear Cache and Cookies**: Clearing the browser's cache and cookies can resolve loading issues.

5. **Contact Support**: If the issue persists, contact Texas Tech K-12 support for further assistance. They can help troubleshoot and ensure that the student's account is set up correctly. You can reach them at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

For more detailed information or specific inquiries, feel free to ask!

Unlike other online proctoring services, Proctorio does not employ the use of biometrics or external human proctors to monitor the student while they take the exam. Proctorio will record the student’s identity via webcam and, depending upon the exam settings, monitor the exam attempt in various ways. Step 2: During an exam Proctorio may take screenshots of the desktop, detect the number of computer monitors connected to the computer, or record web traffic. The information is stored with zero-knowledge encryption, which means the data is encrypted both in transit and at rest.

Step 3: Once an exam is completed, Proctorio no longer has access to this information.

Step 4: It is impossible for anyone at Proctorio or any of its affiliates to view exam recordings. They are only accessible to authorized users at Texas Tech K-12 and through its Blackboard/Canvas system.

**Troubleshooting Access to Canvas with Unverified Email**

If a student is unable to access Canvas due to an unverified email, here are some steps to resolve the issue:

1. **Verify Email Address**: Ensure that the student's email address is verified and correctly associated with their account. An unverified email can prevent access to Canvas and other systems.

2. **Unique Email Requirement**: Texas Tech K-12 requires each student to have a unique email address that is not shared with parents or other students. Make sure the email address meets this requirement.

3. **Check Spam/Junk Folder**: Sometimes verification emails can end up in the spam or junk folder. Check these folders and move the email to the inbox if found.

4. **Whitelist Email Domains**: Ensure that the email domain focusmail.focus-sis.com is whitelisted in the student's email settings to receive communications from Texas Tech K-12.

5. **Contact Support**: If the issue persists, contact Texas Tech K-12 support for assistance. They can help verify the email and ensure the student has access to Canvas. You can reach them at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

**Troubleshooting Bookstore Authentication Issues**

If a student is experiencing issues with the bookstore authentication code or their student ID not authenticating, here are the steps to resolve the issue:

1. **Contact the Bookstore**: Since the issue involves the bookstore authentication code, it is best to contact the bookstore directly. They can assist with verifying the code and ensuring it is correctly applied to the student's account.

For further assistance, you can contact TTU K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

What Information Does Proctorio Collect From Students?

Unlike other online proctoring services, Proctorio does not employ the use of biometrics or external human proctors to monitor the student while they take the exam. Proctorio will record the student’s identity via webcam and, depending upon the exam settings, monitor the exam attempt in various ways. A multitude of privacy provisions have been established to ensure student privacy and FERPA compliance.

Step 1: Proctorio has no file access of any kind. Proctorio cannot and will not access any of your personnel files or documents.

Step 2: During an exam, Proctorio may take screenshots of the desktop, detect the number of computer monitors connected to the computer, or record web traffic. The information is stored with zero-knowledge encryption, which means the data is encrypted both in transit and at rest.

Step 3: Once the exam is completed, Proctorio no longer has access to this information.

Step 4: It is impossible for anyone at Proctorio or any of its affiliates to view exam recordings. They are only accessible to authorized users at Texas Tech K-12 and through its learning management system.

Step 5: Proctorio never stores academic information from any of its users.

If the Proctorio extension shows an error code or won't start, here are some steps the student can take to resolve the issue:

1. **Ensure Browser Compatibility**: Make sure you are using Google Chrome, as Proctorio requires this browser to function properly.

2. **Install or Reinstall the Proctorio Extension**: If the extension is not installed, add it to Chrome. If it is already installed, try uninstalling and then reinstalling the extension.

3. **Clear Cache and Cookies**: Sometimes clearing the browser's cache and cookies can resolve issues with extensions.

4. **Disable Other Extensions**: Other browser extensions might interfere with Proctorio. Disable them temporarily to see if it resolves the issue.

5. **Restart Chrome**: After making changes, restart the Chrome browser to ensure all updates are applied.

6. **Run a System Check**: Use the Proctorio system check to ensure your webcam, microphone, and other settings are correctly configured.

7. **Contact Proctorio Support**: If issues persist, use Proctorio's live chat feature for assistance. They can help troubleshoot specific error codes and provide further guidance.

For further assistance, you can also contact TTU K-12 support at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

answer.text:
**Invalidated Exam and Appeal Process**

If an exam using Proctorio was invalidated, it could be due to several reasons, such as:

- **Technical Issues**: Problems with the internet connection, device compatibility, or Proctorio settings.
- **Proctoring Violations**: Actions during the exam that violated proctoring guidelines, such as leaving the camera view, using unauthorized materials, or other suspicious activities detected by Proctorio.

**Appeal Process**:

1. **Contact the Instructor**: Reach out to the course instructor to discuss the situation and understand the specific reasons for the invalidation.

2. **Provide Evidence**: If you believe the invalidation was due to a technical issue, gather any evidence that supports your case, such as screenshots, error messages, or logs.

3. **Request an Appeal**: Formally request an appeal through the instructor or the academic department. Explain the circumstances and provide any supporting evidence.

4. **Follow Up**: Stay in communication with the instructor or department to understand the outcome of your appeal and any next steps.

For further assistance or specific questions about the appeal process, you can contact TTU K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu. If you need more detailed information, feel free to ask about a specific aspect.

Step 1: In your all-online program, attendance “will” be defined as progress within each semester course.

Step 2: You will have six months to complete each semester course.

Step 3: You must maintain enrollment in a minimum of four semester courses.

Step 4: You must make weekly progress in each course by working in each course a minimum of three days per 7-day period.

Step 5: You must complete a minimum of 5% of course assignments in every seven-day period. For example, if your course has 20 assignments, you need to complete a minimum of one per week. If your course has 60 assignments, you must average a minimum of three per week.

Step 1: Completing the minimum number of assignments does not guaranteed you will complete within the 6-month time frame.

**Reporting Issues with Course Content or Questions**

If a student encounters a problem with a question in the course or content that won't load, here are the steps to report the issue:

1. **Contact the Instructor**: Reach out to the course instructor to report the specific issue. Provide details about the problem, such as the course name, section, and the specific question or content that is problematic.

2. **Technical Support**: If the issue is related to technical difficulties, such as content not loading, contact Texas Tech K-12 technical support for assistance. They can help troubleshoot and resolve technical issues.

3. **Provide Evidence**: If possible, take screenshots or record any error messages to provide to the instructor or support team. This can help them diagnose and address the issue more effectively.

4. **Follow Up**: Stay in communication with the instructor or support team to ensure the issue is resolved and that you can continue with your coursework.

For further assistance, you can contact TTU K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

**Ensuring a Stable Internet Connection for a Final Exam**

To ensure a stable internet connection during a final exam with Texas Tech K-12, follow these steps:

1. **Use a Wired Connection**: If possible, connect your computer directly to the router using an Ethernet cable for a more stable and reliable connection compared to Wi-Fi.

2. **Check Internet Speed**: Ensure your internet speed is at least 1.5 Mbps. Faster speeds are recommended for streaming and online exams.

3. **Limit Bandwidth Usage**: Close unnecessary applications or devices that may be using bandwidth, such as streaming services or downloads.

4. **Restart Your Router**: Restart your router before the exam to refresh the connection and potentially improve performance.

5. **Choose the Right Location**: If using Wi-Fi, position yourself close to the router to ensure a strong signal and avoid interference from devices like microwaves or cordless phones.

6. **Run a System Check**: Conduct a system check before the exam, especially if using Proctorio for proctored exams, to ensure your setup is working correctly.

For further assistance, you can contact TTU K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

My child has an Individualized Education Program (or 504 plan). May he/she enroll in your school?

Online instruction presents different challenges than those in a traditional classroom. The curriculum is rigorous and is reading- and writing-intensive. Successful online students are able to take initiative and manage their own time.

Nevertheless, Texas Tech K-12 strives to offer exceptional education programs that meet the needs of students with disabilities. To qualify, the student's Individual Education Plan (IEP) needs to indicate that the Texas Tech K-12 online program is the appropriate instructional setting for the student and is the student’s least restrictive environment.

The student’s admission, review, and dismissal (ARD) committee has the responsibility of determining whether or not an electronic (online) course/program will meet the needs of a student with a disability. The committee will also take into account the nature of the asynchronous program and what services can be implemented online. It is crucial to note that the program is fully online, providing only services that can be provided virtually as the school does not have a physical location. The Admission Review Dismissal committee will make an informed decision about an online program and the educational appropriateness of this academic setting for a student and his or her particular academic needs.

Is this school a good fit for a student with special needs?

This is the parent’s decision.  Of course, you know your child best and you are the best person to determine the environment in which your child will experience the most success.

Many students with special needs do very well in our online program. Some of these needs that are readily accommodated include:  use of a screen reader, need larger font, need highlighting or color change functionality, need a learning environment free from distractions, need extended time on exams, have social anxiety, have medical concerns. Our online courses are fully accessible and meet Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.0 federal web compliance requirements.

Texas Tech K-12 may not be the most appropriate instructional setting and the least restrictive environment for your child (see above), as required by federal law.

Texas Tech K-12 is a statewide online school district and does not have a physical campus nor a geographic service district. We serve full-time students from across the entire state of Texas.

We have special education personnel to ensure and monitor appropriate accommodations identified in the Individualized Education Program or 504 plan. We closely monitor the academic progress of all students and will provide appropriate interventions and services as identified.

**Requesting Accommodations for Students with a 504 Plan or IEP**

If your student has a 504 plan or an Individualized Education Program (IEP) and needs accommodations such as extra time, follow these steps:

1. **Submit Accommodation Request**: Use the online Accommodation Request Form available inside the Focus Portal. This form allows you to request specific accommodations for your student.

2. **Provide Documentation**: Submit a current signed IEP or a 504 Accommodation Form. The IEP should be from the Admission, Review, and Dismissal (ARD) committee report completed within the last three years. The 504 form should describe any special considerations necessary for taking courses or exams.

3. **Review by Special Populations Team**: Once submitted, the request will be routed to the Special Populations team for review. They will ensure that the accommodations are implemented based on the student's current IEP or 504 documentation.

4. **Course-Specific Accommodations**: Note that accommodations applied to one course do not automatically apply to other courses. Be specific about which courses you are requesting accommodations for.

For further assistance, you can contact TTU K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

Online instruction presents different challenges than those in a traditional classroom. The curriculum is rigorous and is reading- and writing-intensive. Successful online students are able to take initiative and manage their own time.

Nevertheless, Texas Tech K-12 strives to offer exceptional education programs that meet the needs of students with disabilities. We have school all year and do not keep a traditional academic schedule, so it is possible to move through our program faster than the typical semester-based programs.

This is a self-paced program where all the instructional content is provided. The courses tend to be reading and writing intensive. Online courses require self-discipline and excellent time-management skills. The courses are not virtual classrooms and do not require any interaction with any other students or instructors. My child has an Individualized Education Program (or 504 plan). May he/she enroll in your school?

Online instruction presents different challenges than those in a traditional classroom. The curriculum is rigorous and is reading- and writing-intensive. Successful online students are able to take initiative and manage their own time.

It is crucial to note that the program is fully online, providing only services that can be provided virtually as the school does not have a physical location. Step 3: Texas Tech K-12 may not be the most appropriate instructional setting and the least restrictive environment for your child (see above), as required by federal law.

My child has an Individualized Education Program (or 504 plan). May he/she enroll in your school?

Online instruction presents different challenges than those in a traditional classroom. The curriculum is rigorous and is reading- and writing-intensive. Successful online students are able to take initiative and manage their own time.

Nevertheless, Texas Tech K-12 strives to offer exceptional education programs that meet the needs of students with disabilities. To qualify, the student's Individual Education Plan (IEP) needs to indicate that the Texas Tech K-12 online program is the appropriate instructional setting for the student and is the student’s least restrictive environment.

The student’s admission, review, and dismissal (ARD) committee has the responsibility of determining whether or not an electronic (online) course/program will meet the needs of a student with a disability. The committee will also take into account the nature of the asynchronous program and what services can be implemented online. It is crucial to note that the program is fully online, providing only services that can be provided virtually as the school does not have a physical location. The Admission Review Dismissal committee will make an informed decision about an online program and the educational appropriateness of this academic setting for a student and his or her particular academic needs.

Texas Tech K-12’s curriculum is developed to meet the standards of the State of Texas and the Texas Education Agency. The student’s IEP or 504 should reflect that Texas Tech K-12 is an appropriate placement and is the student’s least restrictive environment.

Is this school a good fit for a student with special needs?

This is the parent’s decision.  Of course, you know your child best and you are the best person to determine the environment in which your child will experience the most success.

Many students with special needs do very well in our online program. Some of these needs that are readily accommodated include:  use of a screen reader, need larger font, need highlighting or color change functionality, need a learning environment free from distractions, need extended time on exams, have social anxiety, have medical concerns. Our online courses are fully accessible and meet Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.0 federal web compliance requirements.

Texas Tech K-12 may not be the most appropriate instructional setting and the least restrictive environment for your child (see above), as required by federal law.

Texas Tech K-12 is a statewide online school district and does not have a physical campus nor a geographic service district. We serve full-time students from across the entire state of Texas.

We have special education personnel to ensure and monitor appropriate accommodations identified in the Individualized Education Program or 504 plan. We closely monitor the academic progress of all students and will provide appropriate interventions and services as identified.

Again, as the parent, you will need to make an individualized analysis. We are happy to share more information about the nature of our coursework if that would be helpful in your decision-making process.

If a Texas Tech K-12 student is 18 years old, they are legally considered an adult, and privacy laws such as the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) apply. This means that educational institutions generally cannot share a student's educational records with parents without the student's explicit consent.

**Steps to Share Information with Parents:**

1. **Student Consent**: The student can provide written consent allowing Texas Tech K-12 to share their educational information with their parents. This consent should specify what information can be shared and with whom.

2. **FERPA Release Form**: The student may need to complete a FERPA release form, which authorizes the school to disclose their educational records to designated individuals.

3. **Contact TTU K-12**: For specific procedures and to obtain the necessary forms, contact TTU K-12 directly at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

Online instruction presents different challenges than those in a traditional classroom. The curriculum is rigorous and is reading- and writing-intensive. Successful online students are able to take initiative and manage their own time.

The committee will also take into account the nature of the asynchronous program and what services can be implemented online. It is crucial to note that the program is fully online, providing only services that can be provided virtually as the school does not have a physical location. The Admission Review Dismissal committee will make an informed decision about an online program and the educational appropriateness of this academic setting for a student and his or her particular academic needs.

Minimum Lesson/Unit Completion Requirements

Students demonstrate attendance in Texas Tech K-12 online school by regularly completing assignments. Attendance is directly tied to what the student accomplishes and/or produces over a given period. The assignments completed are the evidence that a student has been in attendance, and if no work is produced, then a student is not considered to be in attendance.

Unless specifically stated otherwise, attendance is required a minimum of 3 days per week. A student must complete at least 5% of course assignments in a seven-day period and in every subsequent seven-day period until the course is completed.

Course completion is required to earn course credit. No partial course credit will be granted. Course credit is earned when the student has successfully demonstrated mastery of the Texas Essential Knowledge and Skills for the course.

Students have six months from the date of enrollment to complete each course. To remain in the program, students must be concurrently enrolled in a minimum of four courses.

Failure to meet minimum progress requirements may cause Texas Tech K-12 to implement truancy processes and may result in your removal from the program.

Yes, international students can apply to the Concurrent Diploma program through Texas Tech K-12 while attending their local school. This program allows students to pursue two high school diplomas—one from their local school and one from Texas Tech K-12. Key requirements include:

- **Course Enrollment**: Students must take a mix of online courses from Texas Tech K-12 and transfer credits from their local school.

Is this school a good fit for a student with special needs?

Step 1: This is the parent's decision. Of course, you know your child best and you are the best person to determine the environment in which your child will experience the most success.

Step 2: Many students with special needs do very well in our online program. Some of these needs that are readily accommodated include: use of a screen reader, need larger font, need highlighting or color exchange functionality, need a learning environment free from distractions, need extended time on exams, have social anxiety, have medical concerns. Our online courses are fully accessible and meet Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.0 federal web compliance requirements.

Step 3: Texas Tech K-12 may not be the most appropriate instructional setting and the least restrictive environment for your child (see above), as required by federal law.

Step 4: Texas Tech K-12 is a statewide online school district and does not have a physical campus nor a geographic service district. We serve full-time students from across the entire state of Texas.

Step 5: We have special educational personnel to ensure and monitor appropriate accommodations identified in the Individualized Education Plan (IEP) or 504 plan. We closely monitor the academic progress of all students and will provide appropriate interventions and services as identified.

Online instruction presents different challenges than those in a traditional classroom. The curriculum is rigorous and is reading- and writing-intensive. Successful online students are able to take initiative and manage their own time.

Nevertheless, Texas Tech K-12 strives to offer exceptional education programs that meet the needs of students with disabilities. To qualify, the student's Individual Education Plan (IEP) needs to indicate that the Texas Tech K-12 online program is the appropriate instructional setting for the student and is the student’s least restrictive environment.

The committee will also take into account the nature of the asynchronous program and what services can be implemented online. It is crucial to note that the program is fully online, providing only services that can be provided virtually as the school does not have a physical location. The Admission Review Dismissal committee will make an informed decision about an online program and the educational appropriateness of this academic setting for a student and his or her particular academic needs.

Is this school a good fit for a student with special needs?

This is the parent’s decision.  Of course, you know your child best and you are the best person to determine the environment in which your child will experience the most success.

Many students with special needs do very well in our online program. Some of these needs that are readily accommodated include:  use of a screen reader, need larger font, need highlighting or color change functionality, need a learning environment free from distractions, need extended time on exams, have social anxiety, have medical concerns. Our online courses are fully accessible and meet Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.0 federal web compliance requirements.

Texas Tech K-12 may not be the most appropriate instructional setting and the least restrictive environment for your child (see above), as required by federal law.

Texas Tech K-12 is a statewide online school district and does not have a physical campus nor a geographic service district. We serve full-time students from across the entire state of Texas.

We have special education personnel to ensure and monitor appropriate accommodations identified in the Individualized Education Program or 504 plan. We closely monitor the academic progress of all students and will provide appropriate interventions and services as identified.

Again, as the parent, you will need to make an individualized analysis. We are happy to share more information about the nature of our coursework if that would be helpful in your decision-making process.

To enroll a student in the Texas Tech K-12 program, follow these steps:

1. **Complete the Intake Form:**
   - Visit the Texas Tech K-12 website and complete the "Texas Tech K-12 Intake Form."
   - This form is necessary for both the Supplemental Program and the Full-Time Diploma Program.

     - **College Preparatory Academy:** For students who meet specific criteria and wish to earn both high school and college credit.

3. **Provide Necessary Documentation:**
   - For the Full-Time Tuition-Free Program, provide proof of Texas residency and a copy of the student's birth certificate.

   - If enrolling in the Supplemental Program, obtain prior approval from your school counselor to ensure credits are awarded.

**Additional Information:**

- **Open Enrollment:** Texas Tech K-12 offers open enrollment, allowing you to start courses at any time and work at your own pace.
- **Contact Information:** For further assistance, you can reach out to Texas Tech K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

Make sure to follow these steps carefully to ensure a smooth enrollment process for your student.

Is there an Artificial Intelligence (AI) Use Policy?

This policy covers any generative Artificial Intelligence tool, such as Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer, Elicit, Photo Math, etc. This includes text and artwork/graphics/video/audio, etc.

All work submitted in this course must be your own. You may not use artificial intelligence tools to complete your assignments in this course.

If an instructor suspects that an assignment is not the work of the student, it will receive a score of zero. The instructor will message the student or provide feedback on the assignment indicating the need to schedule a one-on-one video conference, during which the student will be required to demonstrate their skills or knowledge through an alternative or mutually agreed-upon assignment. The grade of the alternate or agreed upon assignment will be determined at the instructor’s discretion with the highest possible score being 70%.

If it is determined that a student has violated final exam directions on Final Exam A or Credit By Exam Set 1, the exam will be scored as zero. The student may take Final Exam B or Credit By Exam Set 2 with the highest possible score being 70%.

The incident will be reported to Texas Tech K-12 Administration and documented in the student’s file. Continued violations of Texas Tech University’s Academic Integrity Policy will result in the removal of the student from the program. Texas Tech Student Handbook (opens in new tab).

Texas Tech High School Program Requirements

Texas Tech High School: As a full-time Texas Tech K-12 high school student, you must maintain academic progress in a minimum of four courses concurrently. Note: you will need to take more than the minimum number of courses to stay on grade level and graduate at your desired time.

To complete and retain admission as a student in Texas Tech High School, you must work with an academic advisor and be enrolled in a minimum of four Texas Tech K-12 courses (dual-credit and Credit By Exams excluded). Generally, you will complete a total of six to seven credits per year (12-14 courses) and must also pass five State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness End of Course exams to meet graduation requirements.

To graduate with a Texas Tech High School diploma, you will take at least your last year of high school credits (25%) from Texas Tech K-12. Exceptions will be considered by administration on a case-by-case basis but the last semester (2.5 credits) must be taken from Texas Tech K-12.

Is this school a good fit for a student with special needs?

This is the parent’s decision.  Of course, you know your child best and you are the best person to determine the environment in which your child will experience the most success.

Many students with special needs do very well in our online program. Some of these needs that are readily accommodated include:  use of a screen reader, need larger font, need highlighting or color change functionality, need a learning environment free from distractions, need extended time on exams, have social anxiety, have medical concerns. Our online courses are fully accessible and meet Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.0 federal web compliance requirements.

Texas Tech K-12 may not be the most appropriate instructional setting and the least restrictive environment for your child (see above), as required by federal law.

Texas Tech K-12 is a statewide online school district and does not have a physical campus nor a geographic service district. We serve full-time students from across the entire state of Texas.

We have special education personnel to ensure and monitor appropriate accommodations identified in the Individualized Education Program or 504 plan. We closely monitor the academic progress of all students and will provide appropriate interventions and services as identified.

Again, as the parent, you will need to make an individualized analysis. We are happy to share more information about the nature of our coursework if that would be helpful in your decision-making process.

This policy covers any generative AI tool, such as ChatGTP, Elicit, Photo Math, etc. This includes text and artwork/graphics/video/audio, etc.

All work submitted in this course must be your own. You may not use artificial intelligence tools to complete your assignments in this course.

If an instructor suspects that an assignment is not the work of the student, it will receive a score of zero. The instructor will message the student or provide feedback on the assignment indicating the need to schedule a one-on-one video conference, during which the student will be required to demonstrate their skills or knowledge through an alternative or mutually agreed-upon assignment. The grade of the alternate or agreed upon assignment will be determined at the instructor’s discretion with the highest possible score being 70%.

Texas Tech High School Program Requirements

Texas Tech High School: As a full-time Texas Tech K-12 high school student, you must maintain academic progress in a minimum of four courses concurrently. Note: you will need to take more than the minimum number of courses to stay on grade level and graduate at your desired time.

To complete and retain admission as a student in Texas Tech High School, you must work with an academic advisor and be enrolled in a minimum of four Texas Tech K-12 courses (dual-credit and Credit By Exams excluded). Generally, you will complete a total of six to seven credits per year (12-14 courses) and must also pass five State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness End of Course exams to meet graduation requirements.

To graduate with a Texas Tech High School diploma, you will take at least your last year of high school credits (25%) from Texas Tech K-12. Exceptions will be considered by administration on a case-by-case basis but the last semester (2.5 credits) must be taken from Texas Tech K-12.

How do I create a Parent Portal account?

Parents please click here to create your Parent Portal Account (opens in new tab)

Parents, if you have not created your account, please visit our Parent Portal Registration (opens in new tab) page. The Parent portal will allow you to monitor your child's progress in school by providing timely access to both assignments and grades that are entered by the teacher throughout the grading period. You will also have the ability to contact your student's teacher via the "Communications" module inside of Focus.

In order to create a Parent Portal account online, you must have a valid email address. Please note that the email should not be the same as the student's email.

Texas Tech K-12 requires every user to have a unique email address to ensure any communication goes to the intended recipient. Parents and Students cannot share email addresses. The Password Reset Email will not work if more than one user shares an email address. Most ISP or email providers have options for families who need multiple email addresses on the same account for each user.

Prior to starting the account creation process, we ask that if your student has an existing account, you please have their matriculation number and date of birth. The system will request this information to connect the accounts.

For those that do not have an existing account, please click on "I do not have an Account Registered on the Parent Portal but would like to Create One" (opens in new tab).
